entries.title: Fuel system — description and operation
entries.content: The fuel system consists of the fuel tank, fuel lines, fuel strainer, fuel pump, carburetor, and air cleaner, plus an electric fuel gage on the instrument panel connected by one wire to a tank unit. Fuel is drawn from the tank through the strainer by a pump mounted on the forward left side of the engine, which forces fuel into the carburetor bowl until the carburetor float valve shuts off flow. In the carburetor, fuel is proportioned and mixed with air drawn through the oil-bath air cleaner by the action of the engine pistons. Inspect and clean the system periodically; tighten leaking connections and replace kinked or damaged lines.

entries.title: Carburetor — Carter WO-539S
entries.content: Carburetor: Carter WO-539S. Conventional downdraft, plain-tube type with throttle-operated accelerator pump and economizer device. A precision instrument delivering the proper fuel/air mixture for all speeds. The idle adjustment is the ONLY service adjustment provided — replace the carburetor if it requires other attention.

entries.title: Air cleaner — Oakes 613300
entries.content: Air cleaner: Oakes 613300. Oil-bath type, mounted on the right-front side of the dash. Air enters through louvers in the dash side, passes down and across the oil surface, up through the filtering element, then to the carburetor.

entries.title: Fuel pump — AC 1538312
entries.content: Fuel pump: AC 1538312. Diaphragm type, mounted on the forward left side of the engine, operated by a lever against an eccentric on the engine camshaft. Fitted with a hand priming lever on the rear side for priming the carburetor bowl — the lever must be placed DOWN for the camshaft to operate the pump. A filter screen is incorporated in the fuel bowl. Failure to function properly requires replacement of the unit.

entries.title: Fuel strainer — Type T-2, AC 1595848
entries.content: Fuel strainer: Type T-2; AC 1595848. Disk-type (laminated) element with a settling bowl for dirt and water. Located between the fuel tank and the pump, mounted on the right-front side of the dash.

entries.title: Fuel pump static pressure
entries.content: Fuel pump static pressure: 4.5 lb at 1,800 rpm.

entries.title: Fuel tank capacity
entries.content: Fuel tank capacity: 15 gallons (US). Tank is located under the driver's seat.

entries.title: Engine idle speed
entries.content: Idle speed: 600 rpm (equivalent vehicle speed 8 mph). Set with the throttle stop screw after adjusting the idle mixture.

entries.title: Fuel system routine maintenance points
entries.content:
1. Carburetor: only the idle adjustment needs attention. Keep fuel lines, vacuum connections, mounting screws, and choke/throttle clamp screws tight. Keep exterior clean; lubricate all linkage regularly.
2. Air cleaner: check oil level and oil condition periodically; keep element clean and mountings tight.
3. Fuel pump: clean the filter screen periodically; keep mountings and line connections tight. Replace the unit if it fails.
4. Fuel tank: drain periodically to remove dirt and water; keep connections and mounting bolts tight; keep filler cap clean, check gasket seat, clean filler neck screen regularly.
5. Fuel strainer: clean at regular intervals; replace gasket if damaged.
6. Fuel gage: keep mounting screws tight, replace damaged/frayed wires, keep electrical connections clean and tight. Replace the unit if it fails.

entries.title: Carburetor idle adjustment
entries.content:
1. Turn the idle adjustment screw right (in) all the way — do NOT jam it against the seat.
2. Back the screw out between one and two turns (approximate setting).
3. Warm up the engine.
4. Adjust the screw until the engine runs smoothly.
5. Set the throttle stop screw so the engine idles at 600 rpm (8 mph vehicle speed).
Note: this is the only service adjustment on the carburetor — replace the carburetor if it needs anything else.

entries.title: Carburetor removal and installation
entries.content:
Removal:
1. Loosen clamp on air horn and flexible air hose; remove air horn.
2. Remove throttle and choke control wires.
3. Disconnect throttle control rod at throttle lever.
4. Disconnect fuel line at carburetor.
5. Remove carburetor flange nuts and retracting spring clip; lift off carburetor.

Installation:
1. Inspect gaskets between carburetor and manifold; fit new gaskets if required.
2. Install retracting spring clip and flange nuts; tighten nuts evenly.
3. Connect throttle control rod, throttle and choke wires.
4. Install air horn and tighten clamp screws.
5. Adjust idle (see carburetor idle adjustment).

entries.title: Air cleaner oil cup service
entries.content:
1. Hold one hand under the cup and spring loose the two retaining clamps.
2. Remove cup, clean it, and refill to the indicated oil level.
3. Place cup in position on the bottom of the cleaner, push up into place, and lock with the retaining clamps.
Note: in sandy territory clean the air cleaner daily (see First Echelon PM).

entries.title: Air cleaner removal and element cleaning
entries.content:
Removal and cleaning:
1. Loosen the hose clamp and two wing nuts at the centre of the dash.
2. Remove two wing nuts on the right side of the dash and lift out the cleaner assembly.
3. Unfasten the two clamps holding the oil cup and remove the cup.
4. Unscrew the element wing bolt in the bottom centre of the cleaner and pull out the element.
5. Plunge the element up and down in dry-cleaning solvent to wash out dirt; dry with compressed air.

Installation:
1. Install the element in the housing and secure with the retaining bolt.
2. Clean and refill the oil cup to the indicated level; clamp into place.
3. Mount cleaner on dash, tighten mounting nuts and air hose clamp.

entries.title: Fuel pump screen cleaning
entries.content:
1. Unscrew the knurled nut on the bowl clamp, swing the clamp aside, and lift off the bowl.
2. Clean the screen with dry-cleaning solvent and a small brush; dry with compressed air.
3. Blow out the fuel chamber lightly with compressed air and install the screen.
4. Install a new bowl gasket, or turn over the old one if serviceable.
5. Install the bowl, place the bail clamp in position, and tighten securely.

entries.title: Fuel pump removal and installation
entries.content:
Removal:
1. Remove the inlet and outlet lines.
2. Remove the two screws holding the pump to the side of the engine and remove the pump.

Installation:
1. Install pump on the crankcase and tighten the two screws securely.
2. Inspect gasket; replace if unserviceable.
3. Attach and tighten inlet and outlet lines.
4. Prime the pump with the priming lever, start the engine, and check connections for leaks.

entries.title: Fuel tank removal and installation
entries.content:
Removal:
1. Drain fuel by removing the drain plug in the left side of the tank.
2. Remove bolts in the seat rear flange and front legs; lift out the seat.
3. Remove the filler cap.
4. Disconnect the fuel gage wire and remove the fuel gage unit (five screws).
5. Disconnect the fuel line from the tank, under the vehicle.
6. Remove the bolt holding the tank to the wheel housing, remove the tank strap bolts, and lift out the tank.

Installation:
1. Clean out the fuel tank sump in the body and install the tank.
2. Attach tank straps and bolts, plus the wheel-housing bolt.
3. Connect the fuel line; install the fuel gage unit and attach its wire.
4. Set the seat in position and bolt in place.
5. Fill tank, install cap, check tank and connections for leaks.

entries.title: Using the fuel tank filler neck extension
entries.content:
The tank has an extension filler neck to make filling from a container easier:
1. Remove the filler cap.
2. Pull up on the filler extension and turn it to the RIGHT to lock in place.
3. To remove/stow: turn it to the LEFT and pull up.

entries.title: Fuel strainer cleaning
entries.content:
1. Remove the drain plug and drain the strainer into a container. CAUTION: do not let fuel drain onto the cranking motor.
2. Unscrew the cover bolt and remove the strainer bowl and element — do not damage the bowl gasket.
3. Remove the element from the bowl and clean thoroughly in dry-cleaning solvent, removing all dirt from between the disks.
4. Blow the element dry with compressed air — do NOT use extreme pressure.
5. Wash the bowl and dry with a clean cloth.
6. Install element spring and element in bowl.
7. Check element, bowl, and cover-bolt gaskets; replace if damaged.
8. Assemble bowl to cover, install cover bolt and gasket, tighten securely, install drain plug.
9. Start engine, run a few minutes, stop, and check for leaks.

entries.title: Fuel strainer removal and installation
entries.content:
Removal:
1. Disconnect inlet and outlet lines from the strainer.
2. Open the glove compartment door and remove the mounting bolt nuts; remove the strainer.

Installation:
1. Place mounting bolts in the strainer bracket and reinstall on the dash.
2. Install nuts on the bolts through the glove compartment.
3. Attach inlet and outlet lines.
4. Start engine, run a few minutes, stop, and check for leaks.

entries.title: Fuel gage — how it works
entries.content: The fuel gage consists of an electrical indicating unit in the instrument panel and a tank unit in the fuel tank. A float in the tank operates a rheostat, which governs the current flowing through the panel gage. The gage registers only while the ignition switch is ON.

entries.title: Fuel gage tank unit removal and installation
entries.content:
Removal:
1. Remove bolts in the seat rear flange and front legs; take out the seat.
2. Disconnect the fuel gage wire and remove the tank unit (five screws).

Installation:
1. Inspect gasket; replace if damaged.
2. Install tank unit with five screws; attach wire.
3. Check operation: turn ignition switch ON — gage must register the fuel in the tank. Turn switch off.
4. Install seat and bolt in place.

entries.title: Fuel gage (instrument panel) removal and installation
entries.content:
Removal:
1. Disconnect the positive terminal cable at the battery.
2. Remove wires on the back of the gage and the two retaining nuts on the bracket.
3. Remove bracket and take the gage out through the front of the panel.

Installation:
1. Place gage in panel; install retaining clamp and nuts; position gage and tighten.
2. Attach wires — wire to TANK UNIT on the LEFT terminal; wire from CIRCUIT BREAKER on the RIGHT terminal.
3. Clean terminal and reconnect the positive battery cable.

entries.title: Exhaust system — description
entries.content: The exhaust system consists of the exhaust pipe, which for maximum road clearance passes under the vehicle to the muffler located under the right side of the body. A flexible section of the exhaust pipe permits movement of the engine in the frame. The muffler is mounted on brackets with fabric inserts.

entries.title: Exhaust pipe removal and installation
entries.content:
Removal:
1. Remove three bolts in the exhaust pipe shield at the right frame member; remove shield.
2. Remove two exhaust pipe clamp bolts in the skid plate under the transmission.
3. Loosen the clamp on the exhaust pipe at the front end of the muffler.
4. Remove bolt and screw in the exhaust pipe flange at the exhaust manifold.
5. Drop the front end of the pipe and remove from the left side of the vehicle. Discard the gasket.

Installation:
1. Install pipe in position and insert rear end into the muffler.
2. Fit a new manifold flange gasket; attach pipe to manifold with screw and nut, tightening evenly.
3. Attach clamp at muffler; attach exhaust pipe shield with three bolts.

entries.title: Muffler removal and installation
entries.content:
Removal:
1. Loosen the exhaust pipe clamp.
2. Remove the muffler front support bolt and tail pipe support bolt.
3. Remove the muffler assembly, then remove the muffler strap and tail pipe clamp.

Installation:
1. Loosely install tail pipe clamp and support clamp on the muffler.
2. Place muffler on the exhaust pipe.
3. Install bolt through tail pipe clamp and flexible mounting; tighten.
4. Install bolt in muffler support and flexible mounting.
5. Tighten muffler strap bolt and exhaust pipe clamp.
